No. The Moon would not be visible at that time and location.

Its altitude is about **−31.3°**, meaning it is more than 30 degrees below your astronomical horizon in the northwest. Even with a perfectly clear, dark sky and an unobstructed horizon, an object must be near **0° altitude** to have any chance of appearing; atmospheric refraction only lifts objects near the horizon by roughly half a degree, not tens of degrees.

The Moon’s 11% illumination and its modest 38.7° separation from the Sun would matter if it were above the horizon, but here they do not: it is geometrically well below it. You would need to wait until a later moonrise.
